Mara has seen his role expand due to all the injuries OKC is dealing with, and he even started in their last game. With Jaylin Williams (back) out again, Mara could be in line for another start. Mara has at least one block in every game this season and is averaging 1.9 per game this season. The rest of his production has been inconsistent, but he has shown he can be solid on the glass and will shoot a high percentage. He's a good option if you need classic big man stats.

Matković struggled in the Pelicans' last game, but he's still the starting center, which makes him worth streaming. He should be able to provide a little value across the board, as he has averaged one steal and one block over the past week since joining the starting lineup. However, if you're expecting him to have another 25-point game, you'll likely be disappointed. Matković can be rostered until Yves Missi (knee) returns.

Achiuwa's production has been inconsistent, but he has largely been productive as a starter in place of Keegan Murray , who is still dealing with an ankle injury. Until Murray returns, Achiuwa is a decent option. He is averaging 11.0 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.6 steals and 1.1 blocks per game this season while starting seven of their nine games.

articles.title: Tenth Circuit rules in favor of NCAA in Wisne eligibility lawsuit, overturns injunction
articles.summary: In a landmark legal win for the NCAA, the Tenth Circuit ruled in the governing body’s favor in the Wisne eligibility lawsuit on Friday. As a result, the inju...
articles.body:
In a landmark legal win for the NCAA, the Tenth Circuit ruled in the governing body's favor in the Wisne eligibility lawsuit on Friday. As a result, the injunction has been overturned as athletes sought a fifth year.

The suit was filed in Colorado over the summer in light of the NCAA's age-based, five-year eligibility model. Upon implementation, the new rule was not retroactive to members of the class of 2022, and a number of legal challenges followed.

Judge Charlotte Sweeney of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Colorado ruled in favor of the class by granting a nationwide injunction. In September, though, the Tenth Circuit granted the NCAA's request for a stay of the injunction, which meant it was on pause pending a ruling from the court.

Attorneys for both the plaintiffs and the NCAA argued before the three-judge panel Oct. 13. During oral arguments, the judges said one of the central parts of the case was figuring out how the athletes would be harmed if they were not declared eligible.

"It doesn't seem there's been a definition of the market from a huge, huge division – golf, everything," U.S. Circuit Judge Paul Kelly said during the hearing, via the AP . "And you're lumping them all together and you never looked at commonality and interchangeability of the various buyers."

While the court stayed the Wisne injunction, more lawsuits were filed at the state level. The NCAA won out in some of those cases, including in Kentucky, Arizona and Ohio. As a result, athletes in those cases would not be eligible pending a final ruling.

The Kentucky case notably includes Thomas Castellanos , who played four games for the Red Raiders after securing a preliminary injunction. However, after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved the temporary injunction, his availability came into question while awaiting a hearing. A judge then granted a motion for a new injunction , and Castellanos suited up for Texas Tech vs. Arizona State .

The NCAA announced implementation of its five-year, age-based eligibility model this summer. Athletes will now get five years to play five seasons, with their eligibility "clock" starting at their 19th birthday or the date they enroll at a university, whichever happens first.

The Tenth Circuit's ruling also comes as the Protect College Sports Act heads to the U.S. House of Representatives. It advanced out of the Senate by a 77-22 margin in late September and addresses eligibility, among many other issues. The House is not due back in session until after the midterm elections.

If the Lakers share that assessement on Looney—and his removal from the rotation suggests they probably do—they need to start searching for an alternative. Here are three of the best options among logical, affordable trade candidates.

This feels at or maybe above the high end of the Lakers' trade price range given their asset shortage after the Walker Kessler addition. That said, the Magic have never leaned on Goga Bitadze less, so maybe he just isn't a fit with what new head coach Sean Sweeney wants to do.

Bitadze has only seen double-digit minutes in half of his six outings so far. He's also been left on the bench entirely twice. And this doesn't seem to be entirely his doing, since a lot of his per-minute production is in line with or better than his career marks.

He makes a lot of traditional-big-man-things happen whenever he hits the hardwood. For his career, his per-36-minutes averages include 13.6 points, 10.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.5 blocks. He's also a career 56 percent shooter from the field, and he finished better than 60 percent of his field goals each of the last three seasons.

Whatever the Lakers thought Looney could provide, Bitadze actually brings it.

While the Lakers could look for a second-unit version of Walker Kessler, they couldo also seek out a center who adds something different to their equation.

Someone like Karlo Matković, a 6'10" combo big with a career 39.8 percent splash rate from three.

He could open up pick-and-pop possibilities for the Lakers guards or just keep the floor better spaced for their attacks. He also has enough bounce to work in some rim-running responsibilities, too, as he has averaged 1.9 blocks per 36 minutes for his career, per Basketball-Reference.com.

While the Pelicans seem resistant to trade just about anyone—Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones have been rumor-mill regulars for years—a backup big man who isn't guaranteed a spot in the nightly rotation feels like an obvious exception.

If this name sounds familiar, that's because the Lakers tried to acquire Jericho Sims before the season, but they stopped short of meeting the Milwaukee Bucks' asking price of two future second-round picks, per NBA insider Jake Fischer .

Why would things be different now? Because it's hard to set a firm asking price on someone you aren't even playing.

Sims has sat out half of Milwaukee's games so far, and he has only been given seven-plus minutes of run once. He clearly isn't part of the Bucks' plans, but he could part of the Lakers', since he has the right blend of length, bounce and finishing to thrive as an above-the-rim energizer.

Sims has never quite provided enough paint protection to be a true rim-runner, but he is automatic as a lob-finisher (career 74.2 field-goal percentage). Dončić makes more out of that archetype than anyone, so the Lakers could give Sims a second round of consideration.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Domantas Sabonis-Darius Acuff Partnership amid Kings Trade Buzz
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis reportedly has a good relationship with Darius Acuff Jr. despite the fact that the rookie guard's arrival has cut into his scoring opportunities.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis reportedly has a good relationship with Darius Acuff Jr. despite the fact that the rookie guard's arrival has cut into his scoring opportunities.

According to ESPN's Brian Windhorst , Sabonis has "praised Acuff several times and has gone to lengths to support him." Also, sources close to the Kings are saying Sabonis has "taken a liking to the 19-year-old, appreciates his immense scoring talent and enjoys the process of playing with Acuff as he learns the league."

That information comes on the heels of rumors that Sabonis was unhappy playing alongside such a high-volume shooter.

Earlier this week, Sean Deveney of Heavy.com reported that Sabonis was "not enthused" about teaming with Acuff and seeing his offensive role get diminished.

Selected seventh overall by the Kings in the 2026 NBA draft out of Arkansas, Acuff has established himself as an early Rookie of the Year contender with averages of 25.6 points, 7.0 assists and 3.8 rebounds per game.

Acuff is also attempting nearly 24 shots per game, while Sabonis' attempts per game sit at just 8.6, which is fifth on the team.

As a result, Sabonis is averaging just 15.1 points per contest, marking his lowest scoring average since the 2018-19 season with the Indiana Pacers.

While the 30-year-old Sabonis has never been known as a huge scorer—averaging over 20 points per game only once in his career—his shot attempts are his lowest since his rookie season in 2016-17.

With the Kings sitting at 1-7 and looking like they're nowhere near playoff contention, Sabonis continues to be the subject of trade rumors and speculation, as has been the case for the better part of a year.

Despite Sabonis and Acuff reportedly getting along, Windhorst expressed his belief that it would benefit both Sabonis and the Kings to find a trade partner at some point this season.

Windhorst suggested the Kings should do the same with fellow veterans Zach LaVine and Malik Monk as well since it would further clear the way for Acuff and other young players to get the playing time and opportunities they need to develop.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd Announce Breakup, Reveal Split Happened Before WNBA Season
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are no longer in a relationship.
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are no longer in a relationship.

On the latest episode of Fudd's podcast with Bueckers as a guest (starts at 6:38 mark), the Dallas Wings teammates announced they split up and said the breakup happened over a year ago before Fudd was selected No. 1 in the 2026 WNBA draft.

Bueckers and Fudd, who were also teammates for four seasons at Connecticut from 2021 to '25, went public with their relationship in 2025 when Bueckers appeared on the WAG Talk show on TikTok.

After Fudd was drafted by the Wings in April, Bueckers spoke during the team's media day session about both of them being able to separate their personal relationship from being teammates on the court:

"Me and Azzi have always been the utmost professional. We've always conducted ourselves as such, and we've never let anything that happens off the court carry onto the court. That's what we continue to do. Me and Azzi are not new to this. We've been doing this for a long time. We have countless reps at it. We have a lot of experience with it, so we will continue to use that experience to show up and be professionals, great teammates, great leaders, the hardest workers, and continue to show up and do our job and help the Dallas Wings win basketball games."

Bueckers was the No. 1 pick by Dallas in the 2025 draft. They are the first pair of college teammates to be taken with the top pick in the WNBA draft since another UConn duo Tina Charles in 2010 and Maya Moore in 2011.

The Wings won a franchise-record 27 games during the 2026 regular season and made the playoffs for the first time in three years. They lost in the first round to eventual-champion Golden State Valkyries.

Bueckers made the All-Star team for the second consecutive year. Fudd ranked fourth among all rookies with 13.1 points per game and shot 39.7 percent from three.

articles.title: Giannis Skipped Media Availability After Heat's Loss to Warriors Amid 3-6 Start to NBA Season
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo chose to skip his media availability following the team's 120-100 loss to the Golden State Warriors on Thursday night, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo chose to skip his media availability following the team's 120-100 loss to the Golden State Warriors on Thursday night, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick .

"A few hours later, after Curry dropped 29 points and Lendeborg had another well-rounded night (17 points, six assists) in the Warriors win, it spoke volumes that Antetokounmpo made the rare choice not to fulfill his media obligations," Amick reported Friday. "The frustration, for him and the rest of the Heat, is surely building."

Miami has failed to meet expectations this season after acquiring Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks in June.

After the Heat finished at 43-39 during their 2025-26 campaign, they were looking to rise up the Eastern Conference standings by pairing the two-time MVP with Bam Adebayo. Miami also added complementary pieces alongside its two stars, including Tim Hardaway Jr. and Klay Thompson.

The Heat opened this year by losing each of their first four games and have struggled to stay consistent since.

Miami's defensive woes have been particularly disappointing considering their starting lineup boasts strong individual defenders such as Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Davion Mitchell and Andrew Wiggins.

The Heat have allowed over 110 points in every game this season. Their 118.1 defensive rating represents the 26th-ranked mark in the league, per NBA.com .

Antetokounmpo hasn't been pleased with the beginning of his inaugural year in Miami.

"We're not playing hard enough," Antetokounmpo said after a 138-117 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday, per USA Today's Lorenzo Reyes . "We've got to play hard, have some pride. Individual pride, first of all, and then we've got to keep one another accountable and trust one another defensively. Right now we don't trust one another. We're not giving that extra effort.

"Effort, individual pride and trust. We've got to have those three things."

The 10-time All-Star is averaging 27.3 points, 12.7 rebounds and 5.6 assists per game while shooting 56.0 percent from the field this season.

articles.title: 5-Star SG Sydney Savoury Commits to UConn over UNC, Notre Dame, UCLA, More
articles.summary: UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma has secured a top-10 recruit for the 2027 class.
articles.body:
UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma has secured a top-10 recruit for the 2027 class.

Five-star shooting guard Sydney Savoury has committed to UConn over other options including UNC, Notre Dame and UCLA, she told ESPN's Shane Laflin.

Listed at 6'0", Savoury plays for Belleville High School in Michigan. She is ranked by 247Sports as the No. 5 overall prospect and No. 2 shooting guard in the country.

Savoury was named Gatorade's 2025 Michigan Girls Basketball Player of the Year after averaging 27.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and four assists as a sophomore to lead Belleville to a 23-1 record and the DI regional semifinals.

She most recently averaged 27 points, seven rebounds and three assists in her junior season while leading her team to a 25-2 record and DI quarterfinal appearance.

Savoury contributed to Team USA's run to gold at the 2026 FIBA U18 Women's AmeriCup Tournament in June before she was celebrated as MVP of the Nike EYBL Tournament of Champions.

Jared Ramsey of the Detroit Free Press described Savoury as "one of [Belleville]'s main point-of-attack defenders in their trap-heavy defensive scheme."

Laflin reported Savoury "projects as an aggressive scoring guard who can hunt 3-pointers early and often while also creating opportunities for others."

"Her defensive physicality and rebounding will fit the Huskies' up-tempo style and give Auriemma more defensive flexibility," Laflin reported.

Auriemma could now hope Savoury's commitment helps draw other top prospects to the program.

Point guard Kaleena Smith, ranked as the top recruit in the 2027 class, has been connected to an interest in the Huskies. She is scheduled to make her official visit to UConn on Friday, according to CT Insider's Maggie Vanoni .

UConn, which was ranked No. 2 in the AP preseason poll, will look to bounce back from Thursday's loss at No. 5 Michigan on Sunday when it hosts No. 10 Iowa.

articles.title: LeBron James' 'Otherworldly' Basketball IQ Praised by 76ers Teammate, 'It Doesn't Feel Real'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James may not have the same athletic burst he once had, but he has still found ways to leave his teammates speechless in his unprecedented 24th season.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James may not have the same athletic burst he once had, but he has still found ways to leave his teammates speechless in his unprecedented 24th season.

While speaking with reporters on Friday, Sixers power forward Dean Wade raved about James' basketball intelligence.

"His IQ is otherworldly," Wade said. "I've never met a person that has a higher basketball IQ than him... It's shocking how he can sniff out a play before they even get set. It's unbelievable. I've never seen anything like it. He's just an unbelievable teammate and just an unselfish player. The way he passes the ball, the things he sees on the court, is unbelievable. It really is like — it doesn't feel real."

James has managed to outpace Father Time by altering his game: He has become a tailor, and the court has been his atelier. In the latter stages of his career, the 41-year-old has adapted to fit his teammates, his opponents and the league.

When asked for an example of James' intelligence on the court, Wade reflected on a moment early in the season when James was able to diagnose a play and get the Sixers in position to get a defensive stop.

"Like, a team came out of a timeout," Wade said. "I don't remember — it was early. ... I think it was the Knicks, but they came out of a timeout, and he was standing there, and they lined up. And as soon as they lined up, he's like, 'Oh, it's backside! It's backside!' And they ran play, and he called out every action of the play, and that was like his first game. ... It was crazy."

Wade spent the first eight seasons of his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers. He never got to play alongside James, who left the Cavaliers to join the Los Angeles Lakers the same year Wade entered the league, but he was able to witness the crowd's reaction when the superstar returned to Cleveland to play the Cavaliers in 2024 and 2026.

The Akron native is returning to his home state to face the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday night, and Wade expects a raucous environment inside Rocket Arena.

"In my seven years here, anytime that LeBron came back it was just a madhouse," Wade said. "It was crazy. The fans were awesome. So I expect that is what tonight's going to be like."

James has helped lead the 76ers to a 8-1 record to start the season. Although the NBA's all-time leading scorer hasn't lit up the scoreboard, it's evident that his contributions go beyond the numbers in the box score.

articles.title: Taylor Swift gets Knicks’ support after Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride question her loyalty
articles.summary: Taylor Swift may have found herself in a little basketball drama, and this time, it is coming from the very team she was cheering for!
articles.body: Taylor Swift may have found herself in a little basketball drama, and this time, it is coming from the very team she was cheering for! The pop superstar was recently called out by two New York Knicks players, who questioned whether she was a genuine supporter of the team or simply enjoying the spotlight at Madison Square Garden.But just when it looked like the singer would have to deal with the criticism on her own, the Knicks organization stepped in with a public show of support. And its response made one thing clear: the team is not ready to let anyone question Swift’s loyalty so easily.Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride question Taylor Swift’s Knicks loyaltyThe drama began during an NBA 2K League livestream on Thursday when Knicks guards Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride were asked to name the “fakest” celebrity fan they had seen at a Knicks game.Kolek did not take long to bring Swift into the conversation.“Maybe Taylor Swift? I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games,” he said.The basketball player suggested that some celebrities attend games because they want to be seen rather than because they genuinely support the team. He also acknowledged that Swift has a busy schedule and cannot attend every game, but still described her appearances as “a little performative.”McBride appeared to agree with his teammate, although he quickly realized that the answer might not go down well with the singer’s massive fanbase.“Swifties not gonna like that answer,” he joked.Kolek also seemed aware that he could be inviting some backlash, admitting that he might get hate from Swift’s fans. Well, he was certainly not wrong about one thing: questioning Taylor Swift’s loyalty is rarely going to go unnoticed by the Swifties!Knicks officially defend Taylor Swift after players’ commentsHowever, the Knicks organization was not quite on the same page as its players. Following the comments, the team issued a statement defending the Grammy-winning singer and making it clear that she has been a supporter for years.“Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the statement read.The response was a pretty direct defense of Swift, especially after Kolek suggested that he had not seen her at many games. Instead of questioning her commitment, the organization highlighted her long-standing connection with the team and the iconic New York arena.And the Knicks do have a point. Swift’s connection with the team did not begin during its latest championship run. The singer has been spotted at Knicks games dating back to 2014, long before Kolek joined the franchise. Her most recent high-profile appearance came during Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden on June 10.Swift arrived in an orange-and-blue shirt with the words “Stevie Knicks” printed on it, cheering alongside Este and Alana Haim. The Knicks went on to win the game 107-106, making it a memorable night for the team and its celebrity supporters. She had also attended an Eastern Conference Finals game against the Cleveland Cavaliers with her husband, Travis Kelce, earlier in the postseason.So, while Kolek and McBride may have their own opinions about which celebrities show up regularly, the Knicks have made their position clear. And with the organization publicly backing Swift, this little courtside controversy has turned into an unexpected debate about what it really means to be a celebrity fan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: First Friday of November delivers LSU women's basketball setting the biggest blowout record in D1 history with a stunning 40-0 second quarter.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. First Friday of November, boys and girls. It's been a long week. A tough one. But we've made it to another Friday. The Dems can't take that from us! They can take every congressional seat known to man, but I will be damned if they take away a Football Friday. And a Football Saturday. And a Football Sunday. Not on my watch. We're here, and we're gonna lock it in for a few minutes to end the week before starting another big weekend. Let's roll. CBB WITH DANNY Z: KANSAS, TENNESSEE AND USC LEAD ANOTHER HUMAN POLLS VS. ANALYTICS ARGUMENT Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where the LSU women's basketball team treats an opponent like a JV high school team en route to the biggest blowout in D1 college hoops history. Not bad! What else? I've got an incredible national anthem out of Golden State last night, reader mail from the week and Hooters is BACK in NASCAR! What a comeback. It's been a while since Hooters was in the sport after getting evicted from the series last season (true story), but the girls are back for this weekend's finale in Homestead. That's how you end the week strong, folks. I feel better already. Grab you a pencil and scorebook and try to keep up with all the LSU points from last night ... and THEN settle in for a Friday 'Cap! HOOTERS RESTAURANTS KEEP CLOSING EVEN AS CEO SAYS THERE'S MORE TO THE STORY The LSU women showed no mercy last night It's a Friday, the sun is finally out here in Florida after historic flooding earlier in the week, and we've got potentially the greatest Saturday of college football staring us in our fat, American faces. So, we're not beating around the bush today. Let's get after it, and then get on outta here a bit early. First up? I know all eyes were locked in on last night's terrible NFL game, but there was also a college basketball game taking place between LSU and Texas Southern. LSU, for those who don't follow women's hoops, is the No. 9 team in the nation. Texas Southern came into the game 0-1 with a 40-point loss to Tulane. Guess how it went? Speaking of a wild night of basketball ... Lordy. I've never seen anything quite like it. The biggest blowout EVER in D1 history against another D1 opponent. A scoreless second quarter (40-0!). A 106-9 run over the final three quarters. The most mind-blowing stat? Texas Southern went 13 possessions without even getting the ball inside the three-point line in the second quarter. Goodness. YES, ALABAMA'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKING IS ABSURD, BUT ONE TEAM GOT ROYALLY SCREWED BY THE COMMITTEE For those wondering, LSU's NIL valuation sits around $6 million this season — good for second-highest in women's hoops. You'll be shocked to know that Texas Southern's NIL valuation wasn't readily available. Go figure. What do we think? Should Kim Mulkey had let off the gas just a bit down the stretch? Or is this big girl college basketball and Texas Southern knew what they were signing up for? I think I'm in the first camp. I played for the worst DIII college baseball team in America for four years and we once lost to MIT 27-1. I have no pity. Suck it up, buttercup! Next? Let's stay on the hardwood and head out to San Francisco (reluctantly), where the Warriors held their mandatory Pride night last night and kicked things off with a totally normal national anthem: Reader mail & Hooters is BACK! What a week for the left. When you're hot, you're hot! We all knew after Tuesday's bloodbath that Woke 3.0 was inevitable, and the folks out in San Francisco wasted no time in getting back to business. A tiny rainbow flag. During the national anthem. During the actual national anthem. You wanna talk about disrespectful. This makes the WNBA nonsense from last month look like child's play. Woke 3.0 is off to a BLAZING start, folks. Singer Jason Brock ain't backing down, either. "Wow I didn’t interpret it like this, but I wasn’t watching the players," he said in an X post. "Just because they were laughing doesn’t mean it was because of the anthem." It's gonna be a long two years. Heads on a swivel, everyone! Woke 3.0 is officially underway. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL. First up? You know what? It's been a while since we checked the mail. Let's empty it so we can start fresh next week. Yesterday — in honor of National Donut Day — I said the simpler the donut, the better. I'm tired of all these fancy donuts taking over America. Give me a Boston Cream, a blueberry donut, a glazed donut, and leave me alone. I'm all set. From Jerome D: "Have you tried the Sriracha yet? There’s something to a salty spicy donut!!" I love Sriracha as a sauce. I use it all the time (although nothing beats Crystal). But on a donut? Nope. I just can't get into it. I've tried it and it just doesn't work. Next? Earlier this week, I said Wake Forest got HOSED in the first batch of CFP rankings. I stand by that, by the way. The Demon Deacons are overlooked. Luke P. disagrees: "Wake Forrest got hosed? Cmon bud GTFOH. Last 3 games vs a now 5 loss VA team, a now 6 loss Cal team, and now 4 loss NC St team that's interviewing cringy past subway ambassador for HC. Oh before that they put up big on a now 5 loss Stanford squad. I guess we'll find out if wake is real this weekend against Merrimack who has lost to Rhode Island, Delaware, Tarleton St, Yale and Dartmouth but recently fought hard for a W over ...Wagner. ?!?" Fair points from Luke. I can't argue that, beyond the fact that Wake has blown out everyone on their "weak" schedule. No. 4 Indiana, meanwhile, needed overtime to beat Michigan and Minnesota — two terrible teams. Just saying. Finally, let's check in with NB, who did NOT appreciate me mocking the NBA and Luka Doncic the other day: "Why do you watch the NBA if it’s so awful to you? You realize you have your opinions and others are allowed them as well. You have to watch the NBA you have to react to it because your paycheck depends on it. What a sad sad little life you have made for yourself. If you didn’t have these leagues to write about you would be unemployed. Your life depends on the, as you said the "softest league in sports" writing about something you hate is WILD. Hope Fox has good medical coverage because you need a shrink. Have a good day being miserable and letting the world know. I bet it’s fun to know your echo chamber has a few bored people willing to call you out. My huge s–t is done. Wish I could wipe my a– with this article but I’d have to get it out of your a–." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP I mean, do we have the best readers, or what? These people are amazing. What an email! It's perfect. No notes. It's already on my fridge, front and center. FOX, by the way, has excellent medical coverage. OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. On the way out, here are the HOOTERS girls returning to NASCAR for the first time in 18 months. Welcome back.

articles.title: Jason Kidd Pushes Back on Doc Rivers' Giannis Comments, Hypes Heat Star as Top 5 NBA Player
articles.summary: Jason Kidd doesn't agree with Doc Rivers' perspective on coaching Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
Jason Kidd doesn't agree with Doc Rivers' perspective on coaching Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"I don't. I think when you talk about stars, they are hard to coach," Kidd said during a Friday appearance on NBA Today . "But, they want to be coached. Giannis' superpower to get downhill and he makes plays. So understanding Doc saying that his IQ, I disagree with that. I think Giannis understands how to play the game. His forcefulness getting downhill is what it's all about. And so when he causes a problem, he's one of the top five players in the league."

Kidd coached Antetokounmpo on the Milwaukee Bucks from 2014-18, while Rivers served as the two-time MVP's coach in Milwaukee from 2023-26.

Rivers previously detailed the challenges he experienced working with Antetokounmpo in an appearance on the Bill Simmons Podcast (h/t ESPN ).

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers said. "He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it.

"I wish he learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys ... that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shoot-arounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach [Erik Spoelstra] who is as good as there is in execution."

Antetokounmpo blossomed into a star under Kidd before emerging as a dominant two-way force once Mike Budenholzer took over as the Bucks' head coach in 2018, earning back-to-back MVP honors over the next two seasons while receiving Defensive Player of the Year recognition in 2020.

During the 2020-21 season, Antetokounmpo helped lead Milwaukee to a championship while earning Finals MVP honors in the process.

The Bucks eventually parted ways with Budenholzer following a first-round playoff exit in 2023, hiring Adrian Griffin as his replacement.

Griffin helped Milwaukee start its ensuing 2023-24 campaign with a 30-13 record, but was fired in favor of Rivers. The Bucks ultimately struggled with Rivers as their head coach, compiling a 97-103 record across his three seasons.

Rivers stepped down from the role at the end of the 2025-26 season.

As for Kidd, he went on to coach the Dallas Mavericks for five years from 2021-26 before the team replaced him with Dusty May this summer.

Meanwhile, Antetokounmpo is beginning his first season on the Heat after they acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Bucks in June.

Miami has struggled to begin the year, sitting at just 3-6 through nine games.

articles.title: Draymond Green Drops Honest Quote on Kristaps Porzingis' Absence Amid Warriors Winning Streak
articles.summary: Draymond Green told The Athletic's Sam Amick Thursday that the Golden State Warriors have "moved on" from the absence of center Kristaps Porziņģis amid their ongoing six-game winning streak.
articles.body:
Draymond Green told The Athletic's Sam Amick Thursday that the Golden State Warriors have "moved on" from the absence of center Kristaps Porziņģis amid their ongoing six-game winning streak.

Porziņģis, who signed a two-year extension with the Warriors in June, has yet to play this season due to health issues following a diagnosis of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).

It's possible, too, that Porziņģis will not return this season as he announced Friday that he will be stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health.

According to Amick, Green said Warriors leadership most recently addressed Porziņģis' absence when speaking to players after a road trip that ended with an Oct. 28 win at the Minnesota Timberwolves.

"They said, 'Hey, guys, we're moving forward,'" Green told Amick. "'Whatever has to be done with that, we'll handle it. But y'all go play.'"

Green continued, per Amick: "Like I said, everybody's moved on. It's a next man up mentality, right? That's an opportunity for Charles Bassey. That's opportunity for Graham Ike to get more minutes and continue to try to elevate his career.

"So you embrace those guys, and you pour into those guys, to try to help them with all that they can be helped with so that they could ultimately help this team. But you can't sit and worry about spoiled milk."

ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater recently reported the Warriors are no longer delivering salary payments to Porziņģis after "ruling that he is not rendering services."

Bassey, who spent last season between the NBA and G League, first signed with the Warriors in April before inking another one-year deal this offseason. The 26-year-old is now looking to earn more playing time despite missing time with knee tendinitis earlier this season.

Ike, a 24-year-old who went undrafted last spring out of Gonzaga, made his NBA debut with the Warriors after signing a two-way contract with the Warriors in September.

Both players have appeared in seven games amid Porziņģis' absence from the Warriors' 6-3 start. Bassey is averaging seven points and 5.3 rebounds in just under 12 minutes per game, while Ike has averaged five points and 2.4 rebounds in 9.7 minutes.

The Warriors might be looking for a more experienced option at center even if Bassey or Ike earn regular playing time in Steve Kerr's rotation.

The Athletic's Jake Weinbach previously connected the Warriors to a potential interest in the Milwaukee Bucks' Myles Turner, although NBA insider Jake Fischer recently reported Turner is not "high on [the Warriors]' list of potential targets."

The Warriors will look to extend their victory streak to seven games when tipping off their next home game Saturday evening against the Orlando Magic.

articles.title: Knicks defend Taylor Swift's fandom after guard Tyler Kolek calls her support 'very performative'
articles.summary: Tyler Kolek called Taylor Swift's Knicks fandom "performative" on a livestream, prompting the team to issue a statement defending the pop star's support.
articles.body: The New York Knicks are taking no chances with pop star Taylor Swift’s allegiance to the franchise. The team pushed back after Knicks guard Tyler Kolek questioned Swift's fandom, calling it fake, during a stream this week. articles.title: Knicks rush to Taylor Swift’s defense after Tyler Kolek’s ‘fakest fan’ callout

articles.body:
After being called out by New York Knicks star Tyler Kolek for being the team's "fakest celebrity fan," the organization has defended Taylor Swift , who attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals.

The Knicks issued a statement, defending Swift's longtime fandom and her "long history with Madison Square Garden." They are grateful for her support.

"Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," the statement read.

Knicks star Tyler Kolek 's comments about Taylor Swift's fandom

Kolek and his teammate, Mile McBride, did a video for Deflected. They were asked who the "fakest celebrity fan" of the Knicks is: Kolek said there are several "performative" fans who clout-chase by going to games. Among those celebrities was Swift.

"At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative 'cause they just want to be seen at the game; they're not necessarily fans," said Kolek. "Maybe Taylor Swift. I don't know if I've seen her at any other games."

McBride knew Kolek might have made a mistake, saying, "Swifties not gonna like that answer," before shouting out other celebrity fans like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan.

Kolek tried to save himself, conceding that Swift may have "a lot going on so she can't come all the time." Still, he finds it "a little performative."

Swift attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals when the Knicks played the San Antonio Spurs. They famously erased a 29-point deficit to gain a 3-1 lead in the series.

She was decked out in a Knicks-themed shirt that read, "Stevie Knicks." Swift sat alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim. They stayed enthusiastic despite the Knicks trailing almost the entire game.

However, a few weeks earlier, she attended one of the Knicks' games against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals. She was with her husband and Ohio native Travis Kelce.

articles.title: 7 Biggest NBA Storylines Nobody Saw Coming This Season
articles.summary: From the Blazers leading the West to Ty Jerome's MVP-level start, here are seven of the biggest surprises of the 2026-27 NBA season so far.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season has just started, and some of the things happening around the league make absolutely no sense. The Portland Trail Blazers are leading the Western Conference, Ty Jerome is putting up MVP numbers for the Memphis Grizzlies , and the Miami Heat are struggling to win games after trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo .

The defending champion New York Knicks haven't looked great either, Nikola Jokic is having trouble scoring efficiently, and the Golden State Warriors might have found their next star with the 11th pick in the draft. Meanwhile, the Oklahoma City Thunder are somehow staying competitive despite losing several important players to injuries.

Eight or nine games aren't enough to predict an entire season, but there's already plenty to discuss, especially with some teams playing completely differently from what we expected before opening night.

Here are the seven biggest surprises of the season so far, and which ones I could see lasting beyond November.

I had the Blazers fighting for a Play-In spot this season, maybe finishing in the top six if everything worked out , but Portland has started 6-1 and currently leads the Western Conference . They're also running the NBA's best offense, averaging 121.9 points per game with a 122.3 offensive rating and a league-leading +11.2 net rating, numbers I definitely didn't expect from this roster.

Their schedule hasn't been easy either, with wins over the Los Angeles Lakers, Denver Nuggets, and Phoenix Suns, including a 132-119 victory over the Suns on Wednesday. Portland has been moving the ball well, creating plenty of open shots, and getting production from several players instead of depending on the same scorer every night. That's been the biggest difference between this team and what I expected to see.

Damian Lillard has been solid since returning from his Achilles injury, averaging 20.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.1 assists, although his 31.7% shooting from three still needs some work. Deni Avdija has been even better, putting up 23.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 6.4 assists on 47.8% from the field, being that primary playmaker who can run the offense without needing Lillard to set things up.

I love how Avdija is playing right now, especially when he's attacking mismatches or finding shooters after getting into the paint. He had 21 points and 12 assists against the Suns, and having a 6-foot-9 forward handling the ball creates some difficult matchups, particularly with Lillard moving around the perimeter and Jrue Holiday helping organize . Donovan Clingan has also been important as a rebounder and rim protector, giving Portland some much-needed size down low.

The other surprise is that the Blazers have won three straight games without Ja Morant , who suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain . Morant was averaging 15.8 points and 5.5 assists before getting hurt, so losing another ball-handler should've caused some problems, but Portland has kept winning while adjusting its offense around Avdija and Lillard.

I'm not ready to put the Blazers ahead of the Thunder or Rockets in a playoff series, but they're giving us more than enough reasons to take this start seriously. If the offense stays anywhere near this level and Morant returns healthy, I could see Portland competing for a top-four seed instead of spending the season around the Play-In.

Ty Jerome becoming one of the NBA's leading scorers wasn't on my list of possible storylines this season, but that's exactly what's happening with the Grizzlies, where the 29-year-old guard is putting up 27.4 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game. He's shooting 50.4% from the field and 37.5% from three, and Memphis is sitting at 6-2 after winning its first six games.

Those numbers are even more impressive when you remember that Jerome entered the season averaging 19.7 PPG in just 15 games last year, and had a career status mostly as a backup. He had scored 30 points in a game only once before this year, and now he's already had two 40-point performances, including a ridiculous scoring stretch against New Orleans when he scored 17 of Memphis' final 19 points.

Jerome's efficiency might be the most surprising part of his breakout, because he's posting a 62.6% true shooting percentage with a usage rate above 30.0%, meaning he's creating a huge scoring load without forcing too many difficult shots. He's been especially good in pick-and-roll situations, using screens to create space for his floater or finding teammates when defenders try to trap him, and I don't remember seeing him this comfortable before.

The Grizzlies have also given him an interesting supporting cast, starting with rookie Cameron Boozer , who's averaging 16.5 points, 9.8 rebounds, and 5.4 assists. Boozer's 36.4% shooting from the field needs to improve, but his passing and rebounding have already helped Memphis , while Zach Edey provides a physical presence inside and Cedric Coward is contributing 14.3 points and 8.7 rebounds.

Memphis ranks fifth in offensive rating at 118.9, fifth defensively at 108.3, and fourth in net rating at +10.6, which tells us Jerome's production is helping the team on the scoreboard, not just empty stats. The Grizzlies lost their last two games, though, and there's still plenty to fix, especially when opponents start forcing the younger players to make decisions.

I don't expect him to keep averaging 27 PPG all season, but even dropping to 20 or 22 would make this the best year of his career by a huge margin. Memphis has found an offensive leader nobody expected, and if the Grizzlies keep winning, Jerome deserves All-Star consideration.

I expected the Heat to become one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference after landing Giannis, but they're sitting at 3-6, 10th in the standings, and coming off an ugly 120-100 loss to the Warriors . The individual talent is there, but Miami hasn't figured out how to make its roster work, especially when Giannis and Bam Adebayo share the floor.

Giannis is at 27.3 points and 12.5 rebounds while shooting 56.0% from the field, and Adebayo is contributing another 18.6 points and 8.0 rebounds, so neither has been terrible individually. The issue is that both are much better around the basket than on the perimeter, allowing opposing defenses to load up the paint.

Bam is making only 17.9% of his threes, and Miami's outside shooting has been awful at 33% as a team. Andrew Wiggins has been one of the biggest problems , averaging just 8.6 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 1.7 assists on 40.8% from the field and 29.7% from three, which is nowhere near the production Miami expected.

Wiggins' latest performance against his former Warriors team made things even worse, as he finished with only two points on 1-of-6 shooting in 21 minutes. Erik Spoelstra can't expect his offense to work when defenders are already helping off Adebayo and Giannis, and Wiggins isn't making them pay for leaving him open.

The defense has been surprisingly bad too, with Miami allowing 122.9 points per game through its first eight contests and ranking 26th in defensive rating. That's a terrible start for a team with Giannis and Bam, two players who should be providing some of the best rim protection in the league, but the perimeter defense and transition have been major problems.

I still trust Spo to improve the defensive system, but I don't see how he fixes the offensive spacing without better shooting from the supporting cast. And Miami didn't trade for a 31-year-old Giannis to spend the season figuring things out, so if these problems continue, there'll be questions about Giannis staying long-term.

The Knicks were supposed to begin their title defense as one of the favorites in the East after winning their first championship in 53 years and going 16-3 during the playoffs, but they've already had a rough start . They opened the season with three consecutive losses against the Philadelphia 76ers, Boston Celtics, and Orlando Magic, and while they've recovered to 4-4, the offense still hasn't looked nearly as good as it did.

Jalen Brunson is at 25.6 points and 5.1 assists, but he's shooting only 41.4% from the field , and the Knicks are scoring just 110 points per game, ranking 22nd in the league. Their 113.7 offensive rating is only 14th, which is disappointing for a roster featuring Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns , OG Anunoby, and Mikal Bridges .

Towns has been one of their most consistent players with 19.9 points and 13.6 rebounds while making 57.3% of his shots, and I'd like to see him get more opportunities to be the No.1 option when Brunson struggles. The Knicks have the scoring talent to avoid depending on the same player every time, especially with Towns capable of attacking inside and stretching the floor.

The biggest concern has been Bridges , who's averaging just 6.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.0 assists while shooting 33.3% from the field and 29.6% from three . He's playing around 25 minutes per game, his offensive role has been very tiny, and I don't understand how New York expects to defend the championship with a wing producing so little.

The Knicks are also playing at the fourth-slowest pace in the league, leaving them with fewer opportunities to recover when trailing late. Their defense remains there, ranking sixth in defensive rating, so at least they haven't lost that part of their identity.

I still expect the Knicks to finish near the top of the East, but Mike Brown needs better production from Bridges and more offensive balance before I'd put them back among the championship favorites.

The Warriors might have found one of the best players in the 2026 draft without even having a top-10 pick, because Yaxel Lendeborg has been outstanding through his first eight NBA games. The 24-year-old is at 21.5 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 3.9 assists while shooting 50.0% from the field and 40.0% from three.

It's one thing for a rookie to score 20 points on a rebuilding team, but doing it for a Warriors roster that's trying to compete in the West makes Lendeborg's start much more impressive. Golden State is 6-3 after winning six straight, and he's already become one of its most important offensive players, providing the kind of scoring help Steph Curry has needed for many seasons.

His 37-point performance against the Clippers was the perfect example, as he shot 13-of-19 from the field, made six threes, and added six assists in a 124-112 victory. Curry and Draymond were both resting, so Yaxel had to handle a much bigger role, and he responded with one of the best rookie performances we've seen in a very long time.

He's already scored 31 points against the Nuggets and 26 against Minnesota becoming just the sixth player in league history to record at least 100 points, 40 rebounds, and 20 assists in his first five games, joining a group that includes Oscar Robertson and Elgin Baylor.

With Curry putting up 30 points on 42.9% shooting from three, having another player who can score makes the Warriors much more dangerous. I expect Lendeborg's efficiency to drop a little as teams adjust, but he's already shown enough to become a top Rookie of the Year candidate .

Nikola Jokic struggling to score wasn't exactly something I expected this season, especially after watching him destroy defenses for basically six straight years. But here we are, with the three-time MVP averaging 23.4 PPG on some of his worst shooting numbers in years, and the Nuggets sitting at 4-3 despite Jamal Murray playing some of the best basketball of his career.

I already went deeper into Jokic's struggles in my recent breakdown , including how his knee injury might have affected his touch. I still think there's something worth watching there, but what surprises me most is how different Jokic looks when he can't simply score whenever he wants. We're used to seeing him put up 30 points without forcing a single possession, and now he's having games where even getting to 20 feels like a lot of work.

And that's becoming a problem for Denver, because Murray is averaging 25.4 PPG, Christian Braun has been solid, and the offense still doesn't look anywhere near the level we saw last season. Cameron Johnson and DeMar DeRozan haven't given them the scoring boost I expected, Aaron Gordon has been inconsistent, and suddenly the Nuggets are asking Jokic to create almost everything again, except his own shots aren't falling like before.

Now, his 32-point triple-double against the Raptors was a good reminder that he's still capable of taking over games, and I'm definitely not expecting him to finish the year averaging just 23 points. But I do think this is the first time in years that we've had a legitimate reason to question whether Jokic can keep scoring at his usual level for an entire season. That's a strange conversation to have about a player who has made offense look so easy for so long, and one I never expected to be having in November.

At this point, I don't even know how the Thunder are still winning games, because they're missing three of their most important players and somehow have a 6-2 record. Jalen Williams is out after undergoing ankle surgery, Cason Wallace needed shoulder surgery, and Chet Holmgren is expected to miss eight to ten weeks with a right knee injury. That's a lot of talent sitting on the bench, especially for a team trying to compete for another championship.

And Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is basically making sure they don't miss those guys too much, putting up 30.1 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 4.5 assists. He just dropped 43 points against the Cavaliers, then came back two days later and gave them another 42 with eight assists. I mean, 85 points in two games is ridiculous, and the Thunder needed him to go off like that to win both.

The rest of the roster deserves some love, too, because Ajay Mitchell is getting more chances to score, Isaiah Hartenstein is doing his job inside, and Alex Caruso is helping keep the defense together. Even rookie Bennett Stirtz got involved with 16 points against the Cavaliers, and I have to give Mark Daigneault credit for getting this group to win games when some of these guys were supposed to be playing much smaller roles.

Of course, things haven't been perfect, with the Thunder scoring just 110.0 PPG and already losing back-to-back games against Dallas and Houston. They're clearly missing Williams' scoring and Holmgren's presence inside, and having Shai take 35 shots in a game to beat the Cavaliers isn't something you want to see every week. At some point, somebody else has to give him a little more help, especially with those injuries keeping the starters out for a while.

But look, if you told me before the season that the Thunder would be missing Williams, Holmgren, and Wallace and still start 6-2, I would've taken that without thinking twice. They're hanging around the top of the West, Shai is already building another MVP case, and if they can keep winning, they'll be in a great spot for the rest of the year.

articles.title: Kristaps Porzingis Announces He Will 'Step Away' From Warriors in Statement Amid Health Issues
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced that he's stepping away from the team in a statement posted on social media on Friday.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced that he's stepping away from the team in a statement posted on social media on Friday.

"This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn't respond the way I anticipated," Porziņģis wrote in the statement. "I'm doing good, but I know what it takes, and I'm not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself. At this point, I've made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love. In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense. I'm thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support."

The 31-year-old has yet to suit up for the Warriors this season due to lingering effects from his postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).
